chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr from Muawiya ibn Ammar said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Fast Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday, and pray on the night of Wednesday and the day of Wednesday by the pillar that follows the head of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family); and on the night of Thursday and the day of Thursday by the pillar of Abu Lubabah; and on the night of Friday and the day of Friday by the pillar that follows the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

And supplicate with this supplication for your need, and it is: O Allah, I ask You by Your Honour, and Your Strength, and Your Power, and all that Your Knowledge encompasses, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and that You do for me such and such.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended acts of worship and the specific supplication for Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays in Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* prescribes a specific devotional practice of fasting and praying near the pillars of the Prophet's Mosque in Medina on Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays, linking each day to a specific pillar associated with the Prophet or his companions. It emphasizes the spiritual potency of these locations by directing the worshiper to recite a supplication that invokes God's might, power, and comprehensive knowledge to fulfill personal needs. This practice reflects the Shia tradition of *Ziyarah* and *I'tikaf*, highlighting the belief in the sanctity of physical spaces connected to the Ahl al-Bayt as conduits for divine grace.

en.hubeali: Abn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Fast the Wednesday, and the Thursday, and the Friday, and pray Salaat on the night of the Wednesday and the day of the Wednesday by the pillar which follows the head of the Prophetsaww; and on the night of the Thursday and the day of the Thursday, by the pillar of Abu Lababa; and on the night of the Friday and the day of the Friday, by the pillar which follows the place of the Prophetsaww.

And supplicate by this supplication for your needs, and it is, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> by Your<sup>azwj</sup> Honour, and Your<sup>azwj</sup> Strength, and Your<sup>azwj</sup> Power, and the entirety of what Your<sup>azwj</sup> Knowledge Encompasses, that You<sup>azwj</sup> Send Blessings upon Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, and that You<sup>azwj</sup> Give such and such to me’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You should fast on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Perform salat (prayer) during Wednesday night and day near the pillar next to the head of the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. During Thursday night and day, perform salat (prayer) near the pillar of abu Lubabah. During Friday night and day, perform salat (prayer) near the pillar next to Maqam of the Holy Prophet and say this prayer for your wishes. “O Allah, I appeal before You through Your majesty, through Your power, through Your measures and through all things which are encompassed in Your knowledge to grant salawat (favors and compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause) and make my so and so wishes come true.’””
